text:
samir: hey folks :wave: quick question — I rotated my hosted API key on my laptop and now my local dev requests are 401. Should new hires be using the hosted key for day-to-day work or a sandbox/dev key? also curious how people avoid hitting rate limits (429s) during early testing in CI.

devon: short answer: use sandbox keys for most local/dev work, hosted keys for staging/prod. sandbox = low-quota, non-billable, safe to leak in very controlled cases; hosted = production credentials, stronger quotas but billed and should be kept secret.

samir: okay — where do I get a sandbox key? I only see Hosted API Keys in the console.

maria: you can create a sandbox key from the Quickstart page in the Console -> API Keys -> "Create sandbox key". url: https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart (or click your avatar -> API keys). sandbox keys are labeled. Sandbox keys have smaller rate limits but are unlimited for evaling features sometimes.

alex: also, for local dev just set an env var instead of committing:
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-sandbox-key>"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

devon: CI note — never put hosted keys directly in public repos. Use secrets (GitHub Actions secrets, Vault, our internal secrets service). If CI needs higher quota, request a CI quota bump (see docs) or use a dedicated CI sandbox key tied to the repo. Also implement exponential backoff on 429 with the Retry-After header.

samir: where do I request quota bump for my team?

maria: open a short ticket in #devex with: repo name, approximate QPS, and whether it's for CI or staging. We have a template: "Quota request — repo: X, use: CI/staging, requested rps: Y". If urgent ping me and I can escalate.

alex: one more tip — when rotating hosted keys, update the key in the Console and then rotate in secrets store, restart any worker that caches the env var. If you see 401s, check the key in the secrets store vs the Console token value.

infra-bot: :warning: Policy reminder — hosted API keys must not be committed to source. Automated scanner flagged one recent commit in a fork; if you accidentally pushed a key, rotate it immediately and file an incident ticket.

samir: ah — that explains it, I had an old hosted token in my local env file. rotated and replaced with a sandbox key for dev. thanks! :thumbsup:

maria: cool. if you want I can double-check your repo access and set a small CI quota so you don't hit 429s while onboarding. ping me directly.

samir: will do — appreciate it.

devon: quick troubleshooting checklist for others: 1) check which key in env, 2) confirm key kind (sandbox vs hosted) in Console, 3) check secrets store, 4) look for Retry-After on 429s, 5) request quota via #devex.

samir: saved — thanks team!
